Subject: Inquiry: AWS private offer — term + approvals

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick intro this morning. A couple of direct questions as we prepare our procurement cycle:

- Term: Our CFO prefers a 12-month term to avoid long capital commitments, but head of product wants the price predictability of 36 months. Can you outline the pricing delta (rough bands) between 12 vs 36 months for a committed usage profile of ~$120k/year?
- Buyer approvals: Who needs to sign inside the buyer organization to activate a private offer? Our Procurement team (procurement@medignite.com) will push legal & finance, but I want to confirm what signoff AWS/Marketplace requires from our side to complete activation.
- Evidence: We will need SOC 2 & data residency notes to present to our security committee. Can you send a short evidence pack / summary?

Also timelines: we are trying to finalize a pilot and would like activation within 3 weeks if we can align pricing and approvals.

Thanks — Sarah

Hi Sarah — great to meet you earlier.

Short answers up front, then proposed next steps:

1) Term / pricing delta: for a spend profile around $120k/year we typically see 12-month list pricing and a 36-month committed price ~15–25% lower depending on upfront commitment and purchase pattern (steady monthly vs lumpy). I attached a simple pricing_matrix.xlsx with three scenarios (no discount, 15% 3yr, 25% 3yr with annual prepay).

2) Buyer approvals: for AWS Marketplace private offers you generally need:
  - Procurement POC (to accept PO terms)
  - CFO or delegated finance signer (for multi-year commitments)
  - Technical approver for security/evidence sign-off (SOC2 review)
We can work with your procurement team to map who will be the AWS PO signer — that person’s email is often the activation contact AWS expects during private offer creation.

3) Evidence: attaching a 1‑pager SOC2 summary (evidence_soc2_summary.pdf) and links to our compliance docs. If your security committee needs deeper artifacts we can coordinate an NDA + secure sharing session.

Proposed plan (3-week target):
- Today: confirm target term (12 vs 36). If you pick 12-month we recommend a smaller initial discount and an option to extend with price protection.
- Mon/Tue: procurement intro call (we can loop AWS co-sell if you want).
- By week 2: finalize pricing anchor & prepare private offer draft (DocuSign for signatures).
- Week 3: AWS Marketplace activation & testing.

Grace — can you price-check the 12-month anchor and confirm the maximum discount we can approve at quota without escalating? Vivek — can you confirm whether we should include a 99.9% uptime SLA note on the PO for MedIgnite?

Sarah — I’ll put the MAP (mutual action plan) in a short doc and share a DocuSign powerform for the initial acceptance once pricing is agreed.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_matrix.xlsx, evidence_soc2_summary.pdf

Helpful context: they want a quick pilot but procurement is conservative. My recommendation:

- Offer a 12-month term with an option to extend to 36 months at a pre-agreed rate (protects their CFO comfort).
- Approvals: label the PO activation contact as their procurement email (procurement@medignite.com). For multi-year convert-to-commit we’ll request CFO email on DocuSign for finance signoff.
- Discount ceiling: we can approve up to 20% for 12-month at our current quota; anything >20% needs SDR manager + finance signoff. Grace, can you confirm net margin at 18% and signal if 20% is doable?
- SLA: Vivek — confirm whether 99.9% is our standard pledge for private offers or if we should avoid hard SLA language and instead offer an operational runbook.
- Evidence: attach the soc2 summary and provide the secure S3 link if security requests full artifact (we'll require an NDA).

Operational asks: I’ll prepare a short MAP and DocuSign powerform. If they sign within 72 hours we can submit the private offer and request AWS activation within their standard 48–72 hour window. If procurement pushes legal redlines, expect +7–14 days.

Attachments referenced here: evidence_soc2_summary.pdf (already attached to external mail)

Thanks — Evelyn
